notes: cavity rule: latch-up, keyway on the top wide face, viewed from the mating face. Top left. ** THE R/R HALF HAS NO WIRE IN THIS CAVITY ** - confirmed at the bench 2026-08-29 with the mirror-image orientation explicitly accounted for; the R/R half is populated 2x Y + BK/Y only. So the harness brown lands on an EMPTY mate and the R/R does not drive it. The 2026-08-28 conclusion that brown IS the DC output is OVERTURNED - it rested on there being no spare pin, and there is one. The harness-side facts are unchanged: brown is continuous 0.0 Ohm with the switched-ignition net. DC OUTPUT CANDIDATE: a W/R wire leaves the R/R to a MALE BULLET, outside this connector. W/R is the known main power path (B04.6 <-> B06.4, 0.1 Ohm) feeding the starter relay and fuse box, which would make the models' W_RR_OUT (white, RR->SOL) broadly CORRECT rather than wrong on both counts. NOT YET PROVEN - ring the R/R's W/R bullet to B04.6/B06.4 to close it. STOCK, not a substitute - confirmed at the bench 2026-08-29. The R/R carries FOUR leads, in physical order as they exit the body: yellow, black, yellow, W/R. Three enter the 4P (2x Y + BK); the W/R does not - it leaves to a MALE BULLET outside this connector. So the 'no spare' argument holds after all, but on the COMPONENT'S LEADS rather than the connector's cavities: 2 AC in + ground + one remaining lead on a single-phase unit means W/R IS the DC output. OPEN QUESTION worth recording: if this is stock, why does the harness run a brown wire into a cavity the R/R never populates? Likely a housing shared across model variants, or a sense lead unused here. Not a fault, and not resolved. BLADE WIDTH MEASURED 2026-08-29: 5.97 mm across the flat of the MALE blade on the R/R half (the male is the right reference - a rebuild terminal has to fit it). This does NOT confirm 1/4 in: 6.35 mm nominal is 0.38 mm away, outside blade tolerance, so this is likely a 6.0 mm-class terminal and NOT a Faston 250. The earlier ~1/4 in figure was an eyeball estimate and is withdrawn. One reading on one aged blade - measure a second blade, and the harness-side receptacle, before ordering. DEPTH (type 4P rect): 24.5 mm, harness-side body, mating face to back of body. Subtract from length_mm for cut length. ** COMPONENT IDENTIFIED 2026-08-29: SHINDENGEN SH221-12. ** Named at the bench off the unit itself. This supersedes the moulded marks as the part-identification lead - the connector can now be sourced from the R/R's documentation rather than from a mould stamp. TO DO: pull the SH221-12 pinout and confirm on paper that the fourth lead is DC output and that only three pins are populated in the 4P. That would close the W/R question from the component side, independently of the harness ring-out. SECOND BLADE 2026-08-29: 5.96 mm, agreeing with the 5.97 mm first reading. FEMALE RECEPTACLE BORE: 6.76 mm. Profile is the same 'B' section as a 1/4 in Faston, plus a retention tang for the housing. ** THE TWO READINGS ARE SUSPECT, NOT CONFIRMED. ** A 6.76 mm bore on a 6.35 mm blade is ~0.4 mm clearance, which is normal; on a 5.96 mm blade it is ~0.8 mm of slop, which is not. Together with the matching 'B' profile, the bore points at a 6.35 mm / 250-series terminal. LIKELY MEASUREMENT ERROR: Faston blades are chamfered at the tip, so a caliper near the tip reads narrow - and reads narrow CONSISTENTLY, which is how two agreeing readings can both be wrong. Two readings agreeing is not two independent readings if both used the same wrong datum. TO CLOSE: measure across the WIDEST part of the blade body, back near the shoulder, not the tip. ~6.3 mm there means 250-series and the terminal can be sourced. DO NOT ORDER on 5.96. ** RESOLVED 2026-08-29: THE BLADE IS GENUINELY 5.96 mm. ** It is PARALLEL - 5.96 the full length, no taper - so the chamfered-tip explanation above is WRONG and is withdrawn. Two readings at 5.96/5.97 stand as measured. The 6.76 mm figure is most likely the HOUSING cavity rather than the terminal's spring grip, which removes the apparent slop. So this is NOT a 6.35 mm/250-series blade despite the matching 'B' profile. ** AND IT NO LONGER BLOCKS ANYTHING: the SH221-12 is NOT being reused. ** An SH775 series regulator (Polaris takeoff, ordered 19 Aug 2026 per docs/part-selection.md) is on hand, and it brings its own 3-pin AC + 2-pin DC Shindengen-spec connectors. This connector is now ARCHIVAL RECORD OF THE OLD HARNESS, not a part to source. Kept because the measurement is cheap to keep and impossible to retake once the loom is cut.

The one loophole - that the lead might mate a CHILD harness rather than the main loom - is closed by B04.6 and B04.3 sharing a breakout point at B04+200: the R/R's two connections leave the harness together. The SH221-12's fourth lead leaves the body as a MALE BULLET carrying W/R and is the DC output (2 AC in + ground + one lead remaining on a single-phase unit). Four independent agreements point it here: colour W/R both sides; gender male-to-female; B04.6 breaks out at B04+200, the SAME point as B04.3 the R/R 4P; and both run 60 mm, consistent with reaching one component. It also completes the circuit: R/R -> B04.6 -> the W/R net (B04.6 <-> B06.4, 0.1 Ohm) -> B06.4's double-female node -> starter relay + fuse box. ** THIS RESTORES THE MODEL. ** W_RR_OUT is drawn white, RR->SOL; B06.4's node feeds the starter relay. This does NOT rest on continuity, which could not have settled it either way: two unmated halves prove nothing and two mated halves prove only that they are touching. DESIGN CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REBUILD: the rebuild replaces the fuse box and its pigtail with a blade block, so this particular joint disappears on its own. What must NOT be reproduced is the TOPOLOGY - charging output, main fuse output and starter-relay feed all meeting at one bullet junction with a conductor-size step in it. Gauge here is eyeballed, not measured; size the rebuild from the load.

The dimmer's blue common, arriving on a SEPARATE FLYING LEAD rather than through the B02.3 6P. Harness side is a FEMALE bullet. ** THIS IS WHAT RESOLVED THE 6P's OVER-SUBSCRIBED WAY LIST ** - the models had blue occupying a way in the connector, leaving no room for the brown the ring-out found. Blue was never in the connector. BLUE NET 2 - the fused headlight supply. 0.1 Ohm to B06.5 cavity 1 at the fuse box and OPEN to the brake circuit (Blue Net 1). First reading of the B02.2-B06.5 pair was 23 Ohm; the terminal face was scraped and the remeasure gave 0.1 Ohm - both readings are in harness-lengths.csv per the append-never-overwrite rule.

PLAIN BLACK - no tracer. Read off the wire 2026-08-29, which is the only source: the printed switch table renders this conductor as a hatched two-colour swatch that cannot be read, and the models carried BK/W as an explicit guess. The guess was wrong. Individual spade terminal, not in the 6P. BLACK NET 1 - the horn button return, 0.1 Ohm to B01.3's black (the horn) and OPEN to Black Net 2 (the starter trigger). Colour alone would not have separated those two black nets. LEAD COUNT AT THE LEFT CLUSTER: five through the 6P, plus B02.2's blue bullet, plus this spade = SEVEN. The models draw the cluster with EIGHT pins, the eighth being a horn ground. There is no eighth lead, so the horn button grounds through the cluster body and W_HORN_GND does not exist as a wire. Worth one confirming look at the cluster before the model is redrawn.

cavity rule: latch-up, keyway UP, viewed from the mating face, left to right, top row first. Harness side: FEMALE terminals. SAME SERIES as B06.5/B01.2/B02.3 - the 'small' family - which now has four members in this harness. Battery feed. VISIBLY HEAVIER than the harness's common wire - eyeball only, no gauge measured; consistent with it being the main supply into the switch. ** ITS SOURCE IS THE LAST BIG OPEN CONFLICT (W_IGN_FEED). ** The models run white to this pin from the 20A MAIN fuse's OUTPUT terminal - but that terminal carries W/R on the bench, and no point on the W/R net is anywhere near the headlight junction. Either the colour or the route is wrong. ** MEASURED AND CLOSED 2026-08-29: 0.1 Ohm to B06.3. ** B06.3 mates the fuse-box pigtail's white, which lands on the 20A MAIN's W terminal - so this pin is fed from that terminal, and the models' white-from-the-fuse route was RIGHT all along. Neither of the two live readings was correct: what was wrong is that the fuse's TERMINALS were assigned backwards. W/R is the BATTERY side (B06.4's node, with the starter relay and the R/R), W is the LOAD side feeding this pin. So the 20A MAIN protects the ignition switch and everything downstream of it, and does NOT protect the charging path or the starter relay. ** BOTH HALVES READ, ALL FOUR POPULATED, MIRROR 4-of-4, 2026-08-29. ** Switch half from ITS mating face keyway up: R and W on the top row, R/Bl and Br on the bottom. Every pair matches on colour. No dead way here - so the two dead ways found so far (B04.3, B02.3) are not universal, which the variant hypothesis predicts: they should cluster on circuits a B1 does not have. ** CONNECTOR CONFIRMED AS THE IGNITION / LOCK SWITCH ** - by elimination, not resemblance: no other 4-way in this harness carries W + R + Br + R/Bl, and family, gender and way count all agree.

The pod's COMMON GROUND BUS leaving the pod - the four pod lamps share one. BLACK base with a yellow tracer. ** ITS DESTINATION IS NOT MEASURED AND IT IS NOT DRAWN. ** Black base makes Net B the strong candidate, and GND_CHASSIS's own note says most of its inherited leads probably belong to Net B - but that is a colour argument, and colour has been wrong on this harness repeatedly. RING THIS AGAINST NET B (B00.2 / B10.5 / B04.3 / B04.5) before anything is drawn. If it is Net B, the pod earths outside the harness through its own mounting like the rest of that net. ** SPLICE LOCATED 2026-08-29: 1-to-3 inside the POD PIGTAIL's sleeve, not in the pod. ** The BK/Y from this cavity splits into three BK/Y legs. THE CONDUCTOR COUNT MAKES IT EXACTLY THREE, not 'at least': six ways cross the connector and EIGHT wires leave the pigtail into the pod, and five of the six ways are signal (Gn Gy Br LG R/BK), so 5 + 3 = 8. Four legs would need nine wires, two would need seven. AND IT SAYS WHICH LAMPS: three of the pod's four ground locally - IND_L on Gn, IND_R on Gy, IND_HB on R/BK. The NEUTRAL lamp needs no local ground because its return is the LG on cavity 4 to the neutral switch. Four lamps, three grounds, and the arithmetic only closes this way. Same shape of argument as the right-bar 4P, where a conductor count corroborated two splices from outside the sleeve. Drawn as SP_POD_GND.
